title: Lazio's Fuel Mix Diverges: Benzina Slides, GPL and Metano Keep Climbing
dek: As Lazio drivers see five straight weeks of cheaper self-service Benzina, GPL and Metano in the region keep climbing — tracking a steeper rise seen nationwide.
executive_summary: As of November 25, 2026, Lazio's self-service prices stand at €1.9468/L for Benzina, €2.2084/L for Gasolio, €0.8241/L for GPL and €2.1513/L for Metano, drawn from 2,101 of the region's 2,377 registered stations (88.4% reporting). Compared with the previous reading on November 23, Benzina eased 0.25% and Gasolio slipped 0.07%, while GPL ticked up 0.06% and Metano held exactly flat. Against the national same-day average, Lazio undercuts Italy on three of four fuels — Benzina by 0.16%, Gasolio by 0.68% and GPL by 1.09% — while its Metano price runs 1.84% above the national mark.

Zoom out to the 18 weeks of data collected since tracking began on July 21, and a sharper story emerges: Lazio's Metano price has climbed 33.84% while the national average climbed even faster, 40.66%, meaning the region's wider Metano premium over the rest of Italy has been quietly shrinking all autumn, from over 7% in July to under 2% today. GPL shows the mirror image — Lazio's 10.98% rise since July has slightly outpaced the national 9.73% gain, closing a discount that started the summer near 2.2%. Liquid fuels have barely moved by comparison: Gasolio is up just 2.57% regionally versus 2.31% nationally, and Benzina has actually fallen less in Lazio (-0.75%) than nationally (-1.14%). Whichever direction national prices move, Lazio has spent the autumn moving toward them, not away.

fuel_sections.heading: Benzina Keeps Easing, and Lazio Is Outpacing the National Dip
paragraphs: Self-service Benzina in Lazio closed November 25 at €1.9468/L (full-service €2.0916/L), down 0.25% from the €1.9517/L reading on November 23. That keeps the region 0.16% cheaper than Italy's national self-service average of €1.95/L, a discount that has narrowed sharply from where it stood over the summer.

Over the 18 weeks of tracked history, Lazio's self-service Benzina price has eased 0.75% — from €1.964/L in the week of July 20 (W30) to €1.9493/L in the week of November 23 (W48) — while the national average fell further, down 1.14% over the same stretch (€1.9756/L to €1.953/L). The pattern held in the most recent month too: between the weeks of November 2 (W45) and November 23 (W48), Lazio's Benzina dropped 2.81% versus a steeper 3.19% national decline. The result is that Lazio's discount to the national average — which opened near -0.59% in July — has shrunk to just -0.16% today, because national prices have simply been falling faster than the region's own.

fuel_sections.heading: Gasolio Edges Lower in Lazio, Still Italy's Biggest Discount Here
paragraphs: Lazio's self-service Gasolio stood at €2.2084/L on November 25 (full-service €2.3624/L), down a modest 0.07% from €2.21/L two days earlier. That's 0.68% below the national self-service average of €2.2236/L — Lazio's widest discount to the rest of Italy among the three non-Metano fuels tracked here.

Since the week of July 20, Lazio's Gasolio price has actually risen 2.57%, from €2.1538/L to €2.2092/L, a slightly sharper climb than the national 2.31% increase (€2.1747/L to €2.225/L) over the same 18 weeks. In the most recent month, both pulled back together — Lazio down 1.09% and Italy down 1.36% between the weeks of November 2 and November 23 — but because the national price fell faster, Lazio's long-standing Gasolio discount has narrowed slightly rather than widened, from about -0.96% in July to -0.68% today.

fuel_sections.heading: GPL Keeps Climbing in Lazio, Closing In on the National Average
paragraphs: GPL in Lazio reached €0.8241/L self-service on November 25 (full-service €0.8341/L), up 0.06% from €0.8236/L on November 23 — the only fuel in the region to tick higher day-over-day. It remains 1.09% cheaper than Italy's €0.8332/L national self-service average, though that gap has been closing steadily for months.

GPL has been Lazio's fastest-climbing liquid fuel since tracking began: up 10.98% from €0.7423/L in the week of July 20 to €0.8238/L in the week of November 23, slightly outpacing the national rise of 9.73% (€0.7592/L to €0.8331/L) over the same period. The past month alone added another 4.37% in Lazio versus 4.22% nationally. The net effect: Lazio's GPL price, which sat about 2.2% below the national average back in July, now trails by just 1.09% — among the four fuels tracked, GPL shows the clearest case of Lazio converging upward toward the rest of the country rather than diverging from it.

fuel_sections.heading: Metano Is the Region's Biggest Mover — and Its Premium to Italy Just Widened
paragraphs: Metano held exactly flat at €2.1513/L self-service in Lazio between November 23 and November 25 (full-service edged up to €2.2007/L from €2.1972/L). That leaves Lazio's Metano price 1.84% above the €2.1125/L national self-service average — the only one of the four fuels where Lazio runs more expensive than the rest of Italy.

Metano is by far the biggest mover in this dataset: Lazio's self-service price has surged 33.84% since the week of July 20, from €1.6073/L to €2.1513/L, though that's still slower than the 40.66% jump seen nationally (€1.4999/L to €2.1098/L) over the same 18 weeks — meaning the region's Metano premium over Italy, which stood above 7% in July, had compressed to under 2% by late November. But the most recent month tells a smaller, different story: from the week of November 2 to the week of November 23, Lazio's Metano climbed 3.01% (€2.0884/L to €2.1513/L, then plateaued) while the national average rose just 1.87% (€2.071/L to €2.1098/L) — a sign that the long compression of Lazio's Metano premium may be stabilizing rather than continuing to narrow.

network_section.heading: 2,101 of 2,377 Lazio Stations Reporting Today
paragraphs: Lazio counts 2,377 registered fuel stations in the MIMIT registry, of which 2,101 reported at least one price today — an 88.4% reporting rate, essentially unchanged from the 88.5% rate (2,104 of 2,377) recorded on November 23.

That reporting rate trails the national figure of 90.5% (21,685 of 23,974 stations reporting), a gap of roughly two percentage points. A reporting rate below 100% is normal — not every station updates its prices to MIMIT every single day — but a persistently lower rate in a region means the mix of stations behind the daily average shifts slightly from one day to the next, which is worth keeping in mind when reading small day-over-day moves.

methodology_section.heading: Built by an Unattended Pipeline, Not a Spreadsheet
paragraphs: Every part of this report — the underlying price and station-registry data, the region-of-the-day rotation, the week-by-week trend analysis above, and the prose itself — is produced automatically each morning by an unattended pipeline built with Claude Code. A scheduled agent pulls the latest MIMIT fuel-price feed (or a locally downloaded CSV when one is available), recomputes national and regional averages, deterministically selects which of Italy's 20 regions gets today's spotlight, and writes this report, the live dashboard's data, and this Word document without a person approving the content before it is published.

That's a deliberate contrast with how a report like this traditionally gets made — a manually maintained spreadsheet that someone has to open, update, recalculate and write up by hand every single day, with all the lag and error that implies. Fuel Dashboard instead treats daily fuel-price reporting the way a market would treat a daily close: a number that gets reported, a pipeline that captures it, and a system that narrates it the same day without waiting on a human in the loop.

closing.heading: Explore Beyond Lazio and Agip Eni
paragraphs: The live Fuel Dashboard (https://adeo-blip.github.io/fuel-price-italy/) opens by default on Agip Eni's brand-level view, but that's just one slice of the data. Use the scope picker to switch to Region and pull up Lazio's full daily history, to Province or Municipality for hyper-local detail, or to Operator/Brand to compare any of the other brands tracked nationwide — the same underlying dataset behind this report powers all of it.

pull_quote: Since late July, self-service Metano in Lazio has jumped nearly 34% — but that's still slower than the 41% surge seen across Italy as a whole.
caption:
Today's Fuel Dashboard spotlight: Lazio. Self-service Benzina is down to €1.9468/L and Gasolio to €2.2084/L, both a touch cheaper than the Italian average — but Metano is the real story. Lazio's Metano price has jumped nearly 34% since late July, and while that's actually a slower climb than the 41% rise seen nationwide, it still leaves the region about 1.8% above the rest of Italy on Metano today.

Fuel Dashboard tracks self-service and full-service prices for Benzina, Gasolio, GPL and Metano across all 20 Italian regions, every province, every municipality, and 300+ brands, using Italy's MIMIT daily price feed. The dashboard, the daily regional spotlight report, and even the words you're reading right now are generated automatically, every single day, by an unattended pipeline built with Claude Code — no spreadsheet, no manual update, no one copying numbers into Excel every morning.

That's the real pitch here: a self-updating, interactive dashboard with real trend analysis beats a static spreadsheet not because it looks nicer, but because it never goes stale and never needs someone to maintain it. If you're curious what that looks like for Italian fuel prices, or want to compare any region, province or brand yourself, visit the live dashboard: https://adeo-blip.github.io/fuel-price-italy/
